page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Running on a KVM hypervisor, this instance provides 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place the ecs.hfg6.4xlarge consistently in the average tier across multiple workloads. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is recorded at 1439.19, while the multi-core score reaches 15350.78. Memory bandwidth tests yield 855.0 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 90.64 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. In application-specific benchmarks, the instance achieves a static web serving throughput of 12.4 GB/sec and processes 15.39 million Redis SET operations per second. For LLM inference workloads, the server handles prompt processing for a small 135M model at 942.59 tokens/sec, though performance drops to a weak rating of 23.22 tokens/sec for prompt processing on a medium 7B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offer stable, predictable performance for production workloads without the risk of resource contention. However, the lack of bundled local storage means users must provision external block storage, which introduces a performance and cost tradeoff depending on the required IOPS. The absence of a GPU also limits its utility for heavy deep learning training. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, database operations, software compilation, and moderate-scale text or image processing.
